subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Coordination Games and Focal Points
description: A short lesson to help you apply Coordination Games and Focal Points.

hook.text: You must meet a stranger in New York City with no way to communicate. Most people independently choose Grand Central.

buildup.text: Coordination Games and Focal Points sets up the incentives, biases, and tradeoffs driving the choice.

discovery.text: Schelling found people use focal points: culturally prominent choices that stand out.

twist.text: Focal points are culturally specific. A Japanese pair might pick Shibuya Crossing.

climax.text: Coordination Games and Focal Points matters because better design changes real decisions.

punchline.text: Without words, we find each other through shared expectations.

quiz.question: What is a focal point in game theory?
options: The optimal mathematical solution to a game
A culturally prominent choice that players independently gravitate toward
The point where both players decide to stop playing
